thread:
emily: Customer reported SSO logins failing after their IdP cert rotation. Getting 403s at our ACS with 'RecipientNotFound' and 'InvalidDestination'. They say it started immediately after cert swap.

sanjay: Can you paste the raw SAML Response (redact user ids) and the ACS URL it's destined for?

emily: Pasted redacted assertion below. Destination shows query param and host that looks like CDN rewrite.
```xml
<samlp:Response Destination=\"https://acme-cdn.example.com/saml/acs?tenant=acme\" ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>...
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```

maya: That Destination includes the CDN hostname. Our recipient matching expects the SP's canonical host (login.redwood.dev) and fails if Host header was rewritten. Could be the CDN rewriting Host -> acme-cdn.example.com after rotation triggered their edge rules. :thinking_face:

liam: Any errors from our metadata loader? Maybe the metadata poller picked up the new cert but the customer still has an older cached chain somewhere.

emily: Logs from the auth service: `saml: recipient mismatch: expected https://login.redwood.dev/saml/acs but got https://acme-cdn.example.com/saml/acs?tenant=acme` and later `signature verification OK for key id 0x1234`. So signature matches but recipient compare fails.

sanjay: Steps to reproduce locally? emily, can you try hitting our ACS with Host header set to acme-cdn.example.com and confirm the match failure?

emily: Repro command I ran: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST 'https://login.redwood.dev/saml/acs?tenant=acme' \
  -H 'Host: acme-cdn.example.com' \
  --data-binary @redacted_response.xml -v
```
Response is 403 with the recipient mismatch we saw.

maya: Quick mitigation: enable metadata refresh for that tenant immediately and clear the runtime cache for that SP. I pushed a cache flush button for tenant `acme` (internal). Asking them to retry.

emily: I asked customer to retry — they still hit 403. They said CDN will continue rewriting host for now.

ashley: Two options: 1) Accept the rewritten host as an allowed recipient for that tenant (config entry), 2) Add logic to normalize recipient comparison to ignore host header differences when a trusted proxy header is present. Both have security implications.

sanjay: For short-term we should add a tenant-level allowed-recipient alias. I can add it to the tenant config: `allowed_acmecdn_hostnames: [\"acme-cdn.example.com\"]`. That avoids code change. emily, do you have permission to update tenant config?

emily: I don't. Need eng or platform to patch.

liam: I'll create a temporary flag in the admin console and enable it for acme. Doing now. branch: `hotfix/accept-acme-cdn-host-6881`. deploy-bot: please standby for canary.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for hotfix/accept-acme-cdn-host-6881 to `auth-service` (canary=1%).

metadata-watcher-bot: IdP metadata for tenant `acme` refreshed at 2026-03-17T15:10:22Z (picked up new cert chain). Poller interval is 5m.

emily: After canary, customer retried and login succeeded for a small subset of users. :thumbsup: They report intermittent 403s for edge cases that contain `?tenant=` in the query.

maya: Looks like our recipient normalizer currently strips querystring for some checks but not all code paths. We need a proper fix: normalize Destination URLs (strip CDN host if in allowed list and remove insignificant query params) and centralize recipient matching. Filing an ENG ticket.

ashley: Create an incident/engineering ticket with repro steps and example SAML (redacted), include the curl command above, and mark priority P1 for customer impact.

liam: Ticket created: INFRA-1829 "recipient matching: accept trusted host rewrites and normalize destination queries". Assigned to eng-sso team.

sanjay: Temporary action summary for support: 1) Add tenant allowed hostname alias, 2) instruct customer to set `X-Forwarded-Host` to original host (if their CDN supports it) or disable host rewrite, 3) monitor for failed assertions in the next 2 hours and escalate if rate > 1% of logins.

emily: Communicated steps to customer. They applied alias and confirmed majority of users can login. Leaving ticket open for eng fix. :white_check_mark:

liam: Engineering next steps: implement canonical recipient normalizer, add unit tests for querystring handling, and add an opt-in tenant policy to allow host aliasing. Planned for next patch release (patch/2026-03-20).

maya: I'll add a short KB article for support with the curl repro and mitigation steps so we don't repeat manual changes.

emily: Closing loop with customer, keeping live incident for eng until patch is shipped.

ashley: Nice triage everyone. Documented timeline in the incident notes. :sparkles:
